tensorflow/tensorflow.what_it_does: TensorFlow is an open-source machine learning framework from Google for building, training and deploying models, from research prototypes to production systems on servers, mobile and the browser.
tensorflow/tensorflow.why_it_matters: It is one of the two foundational deep-learning frameworks, with a large ecosystem (Keras, TFLite, TF Serving) that many production ML systems still run on.
tensorflow/tensorflow.when_to_use: When you are deploying to mobile or edge through TFLite, or maintaining an existing TensorFlow or Keras codebase.
key_superpowers: TensorFlow Lite for mobile and edge

ollama/ollama.what_it_does: Ollama runs open-weight language models on your own machine. You pull a model with one command and it serves a local API that other tools can call.
ollama/ollama.why_it_matters: It made local model serving a one-command task, and many agent frameworks and chat apps now default to talking to an Ollama endpoint.
ollama/ollama.when_to_use: When you want a private, local model endpoint with minimal setup, for chat, coding assistants or testing an agent without a cloud API key.
key_superpowers: Runs on macOS, Linux and Windows

langchain-ai/langchain.what_it_does: LangChain is a framework for building applications on top of language models. It provides components for prompts, model calls, retrieval, tools and chains of steps.
langchain-ai/langchain.why_it_matters: It is one of the most widely used LLM application frameworks, with integrations for most model providers and vector stores.
langchain-ai/langchain.when_to_use: When you want ready-made integrations and standard building blocks for a retrieval or tool-using LLM app, and are happy with a larger abstraction layer.
key_superpowers: Hundreds of provider and vector store integrations
Pairs with LangGraph for stateful agents

langgenius/dify.what_it_does: Dify is an open-source platform for building LLM apps visually. It combines a workflow editor, a RAG pipeline, agents and model management in one self-hostable app.
langgenius/dify.why_it_matters: It lets teams prototype and operate LLM apps without writing orchestration code, and it exposes apps as APIs.
langgenius/dify.when_to_use: When non-engineers need to build or edit LLM workflows, or you want a self-hosted alternative to hosted app builders.

langflow-ai/langflow.what_it_does: Langflow is a visual builder for LLM agents and workflows. You connect components on a canvas, then run the flow or export it as an API.
langflow-ai/langflow.why_it_matters: It makes agent pipelines easy to inspect and iterate on visually, and flows can be served as endpoints.
langflow-ai/langflow.when_to_use: When you want to design and debug an agent or RAG flow on a canvas before moving it into code.

open-webui/open-webui.what_it_does: Open WebUI is a self-hosted chat interface for LLMs. It works with local models through Ollama and with OpenAI-compatible APIs, and adds features such as RAG over documents.
open-webui/open-webui.why_it_matters: It is a widely used front end that gives a ChatGPT-style experience over local or self-hosted models.
open-webui/open-webui.when_to_use: When you want a multi-user, self-hosted chat UI in front of Ollama or other OpenAI-compatible endpoints.
key_superpowers: Works with Ollama and OpenAI-compatible APIs

comfy-org/comfyui.what_it_does: ComfyUI is a node-based interface and backend for diffusion models. You build image and video generation pipelines as graphs of nodes.
comfy-org/comfyui.why_it_matters: It exposes the internals of Stable Diffusion-style pipelines, so advanced users can build and share complex workflows.
comfy-org/comfyui.when_to_use: When you need fine control over an image or video generation pipeline, or want to reuse shared node workflows.

automatic1111/stable-diffusion-webui.what_it_does: Stable Diffusion web UI is a browser interface for running Stable Diffusion image generation locally, with text-to-image, image-to-image, inpainting and extensions.
automatic1111/stable-diffusion-webui.why_it_matters: It was one of the first widely used local image generation front ends, and it has a large extension library.
automatic1111/stable-diffusion-webui.when_to_use: When you want a familiar form-based UI for local Stable Diffusion work and its extensions.

huggingface/transformers.what_it_does: Transformers is Hugging Face's library of pretrained model architectures for text, vision, audio and multimodal tasks, with a common API for loading, fine-tuning and running them.
huggingface/transformers.why_it_matters: It is the standard way to load open models from the Hugging Face Hub and is a dependency of much of the open-model ecosystem.
huggingface/transformers.when_to_use: When you want to load, fine-tune or run an open model from the Hub using PyTorch, JAX or TensorFlow.
key_superpowers: Tens of thousands of Hub checkpoints
Training and inference in one library

vllm-project/vllm.what_it_does: vLLM is a high-throughput inference and serving engine for large language models. It uses paged attention and continuous batching to serve many requests efficiently on GPUs.
vllm-project/vllm.why_it_matters: It is one of the standard choices for production LLM serving, with an OpenAI-compatible server.
vllm-project/vllm.when_to_use: When you serve an open model to many concurrent users on GPU hardware and throughput matters.

anthropics/claude-code.what_it_does: Claude Code is Anthropic's agentic coding tool for the terminal. It reads your codebase, edits files and runs commands on your behalf, with your approval for actions.
anthropics/claude-code.why_it_matters: It is a widely used example of a terminal coding agent that works across a whole repository, not just single snippets.
anthropics/claude-code.when_to_use: When you want an AI agent to make multi-file changes, run tests and work through a task in your existing repository.
key_superpowers: Runs shell commands with permission prompts

openai/codex.what_it_does: Codex CLI is OpenAI's lightweight coding agent that runs in your terminal. It reads and edits code in your project and runs commands, with configurable approval modes.
openai/codex.why_it_matters: It brings a coding agent into the terminal in a small open-source package.
openai/codex.when_to_use: When you want a terminal coding agent with a lightweight install and configurable approval levels.

browser-use/browser-use.what_it_does: Browser Use lets an LLM agent control a web browser to complete tasks such as navigating sites, filling forms and extracting data.
browser-use/browser-use.why_it_matters: It is a popular open-source layer for giving agents browser control, with a model-agnostic design.
browser-use/browser-use.when_to_use: When an agent must act on websites that have no API, for example to fill forms or collect data from pages.

openai/whisper.what_it_does: Whisper is OpenAI's open-source speech recognition model. It transcribes and translates speech in many languages and runs locally.
openai/whisper.why_it_matters: It set a strong open baseline for multilingual speech recognition and spawned many faster derivatives.
openai/whisper.when_to_use: When you need offline transcription or multilingual speech-to-text without a cloud API.

google-gemini/gemini-cli.what_it_does: Gemini CLI is an open-source AI agent for the terminal from Google that uses Gemini models to help with coding and other tasks in your shell.
google-gemini/gemini-cli.why_it_matters: It is a widely used open-source terminal agent backed by a hosted frontier model.
google-gemini/gemini-cli.when_to_use: When you want a terminal agent for code and file tasks using Gemini models.

rasbt/llms-from-scratch.what_it_does: LLMs-from-scratch is Sebastian Raschka's companion code for the book of the same name. It implements a GPT-style language model step by step in PyTorch.
rasbt/llms-from-scratch.why_it_matters: It is one of the most used hands-on resources for understanding how transformer LLMs are built, with runnable code for each chapter.
rasbt/llms-from-scratch.when_to_use: When you want to learn how an LLM works internally by building one yourself.

pytorch/pytorch.what_it_does: PyTorch is an open-source deep-learning framework with tensor computation on GPUs and automatic differentiation for building and training neural networks.
pytorch/pytorch.why_it_matters: It is the most widely used framework for AI research and a common base for production model training and inference.
pytorch/pytorch.when_to_use: When you are building or training neural networks, or working with most open-model code on the Hub.

infiniflow/ragflow.what_it_does: RAGFlow is an open-source retrieval-augmented generation engine. It parses documents with layout-aware chunking, indexes them, and answers questions with cited sources.
infiniflow/ragflow.why_it_matters: It packages document parsing, retrieval and citations into one deployable engine, which saves teams building RAG from scratch.
infiniflow/ragflow.when_to_use: When you need a self-hosted document Q&A system with citations over PDFs and office files.

opencv/opencv.what_it_does: OpenCV is an open-source computer vision library with image processing, video analysis, camera calibration and many classical and deep-learning-based algorithms.
opencv/opencv.why_it_matters: It is the standard library for practical computer vision work across languages and platforms.
opencv/opencv.when_to_use: When you need image or video processing, detection pipelines or camera tools in an application.
key_superpowers: Bindings for C++, Python and Java

modelcontextprotocol/servers.what_it_does: This repository holds reference Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers that give AI assistants standard access to tools and data such as files, git and search.
modelcontextprotocol/servers.why_it_matters: It is the reference set of MCP servers that shows how to expose tools to any MCP-compatible client.
modelcontextprotocol/servers.when_to_use: When you want an assistant to reach a common data source through a ready MCP server, or to learn how to write one.

paddlepaddle/paddleocr.what_it_does: PaddleOCR is an open-source OCR and document-parsing toolkit that extracts text, tables and layout from images and PDFs into structured output.
paddlepaddle/paddleocr.why_it_matters: It is one of the strongest open OCR toolkits, with multilingual models and document-parsing pipelines.
paddlepaddle/paddleocr.when_to_use: When you need to turn scanned documents or images into text or structured data, including for multilingual content.

openhands/openhands.what_it_does: OpenHands is an open-source platform for AI software-development agents. Agents write code, run commands and browse the web inside a sandbox.
openhands/openhands.why_it_matters: It is a widely used open platform for running autonomous coding agents with a sandboxed environment.
openhands/openhands.when_to_use: When you want an agent to attempt development tasks in an isolated sandbox rather than in your own shell.

unclecode/crawl4ai.what_it_does: Crawl4AI is an open-source web crawler that converts pages into clean, LLM-ready Markdown, including JavaScript-rendered pages.
unclecode/crawl4ai.why_it_matters: It fills a common gap in RAG and agent pipelines: turning messy web pages into text that a model can use.
unclecode/crawl4ai.when_to_use: When you need to collect web content for retrieval or agent use and want self-hosted crawling.

hiyouga/llamafactory.what_it_does: LLaMA-Factory is a toolkit for fine-tuning more than 100 large language and vision-language models, with a web UI and support for common methods such as LoRA and QLoRA.
hiyouga/llamafactory.why_it_matters: It makes fine-tuning many open models practical through one tool, instead of a different script per model family.
hiyouga/llamafactory.when_to_use: When you want to fine-tune an open model on your own data without writing training code from scratch.

unslothai/unsloth.what_it_does: Unsloth is a library and local UI for fine-tuning and running LLMs and diffusion models, with optimized kernels that reduce training memory and time.
unslothai/unsloth.why_it_matters: It lowers the hardware needed for fine-tuning open models, which makes single-GPU work practical.
unslothai/unsloth.when_to_use: When you fine-tune a model on limited GPU memory and want a fast, low-memory path.

nomic-ai/gpt4all.what_it_does: GPT4All is a desktop application and library for running open-weight language models locally on consumer hardware, with a chat interface and local document search.
nomic-ai/gpt4all.why_it_matters: It is one of the earliest and most accessible ways for non-developers to run local models.
nomic-ai/gpt4all.when_to_use: When you want a simple desktop app to chat with a local model and query your own documents without setup.

opendatalab/mineru.what_it_does: MinerU converts PDFs and office documents into Markdown or JSON for LLM pipelines, keeping layout, tables and formulas.
opendatalab/mineru.why_it_matters: It addresses the document-parsing step that RAG and agent systems often get wrong.
opendatalab/mineru.when_to_use: When you need clean structured text from complex PDFs for retrieval or model input.

dair-ai/prompt-engineering-guide.what_it_does: The Prompt Engineering Guide is an open collection of guides, papers summaries, lessons and notebooks on prompting, context engineering, RAG and agents.
dair-ai/prompt-engineering-guide.why_it_matters: It is one of the most referenced free learning resources on prompting techniques.
dair-ai/prompt-engineering-guide.when_to_use: When you want to learn prompting techniques or find papers and examples on a specific method.

mlabonne/llm-course.what_it_does: LLM Course is a free course with roadmaps and Colab notebooks for learning large language models, from fundamentals to deployment.
mlabonne/llm-course.why_it_matters: It is a widely used structured path for people moving into LLM engineering.
mlabonne/llm-course.when_to_use: When you want a guided, notebook-based route into LLMs with hands-on exercises.

microsoft/ai-agents-for-beginners.what_it_does: AI Agents for Beginners is a Microsoft course of 18 lessons with code samples, covering how to design and build AI agents.
microsoft/ai-agents-for-beginners.why_it_matters: It is a structured free introduction to agent design from a major vendor.
microsoft/ai-agents-for-beginners.when_to_use: When you are new to agents and want a guided course with code.

microsoft/generative-ai-for-beginners.what_it_does: Generative AI for Beginners is a Microsoft course of 21 lessons with code samples, covering the basics of building apps on generative AI models.
microsoft/generative-ai-for-beginners.why_it_matters: It is a widely used structured introduction to generative AI for developers.
microsoft/generative-ai-for-beginners.when_to_use: When you want a guided introduction to generative AI app development with code.

openai/openai-cookbook.what_it_does: The OpenAI Cookbook is a collection of example code and guides for using the OpenAI API for tasks such as embeddings, retrieval, function calling and evaluation.
openai/openai-cookbook.why_it_matters: It is a widely used set of practical, runnable recipes for API integration.
openai/openai-cookbook.when_to_use: When you want working examples for a specific OpenAI API feature.
key_superpowers: Covers embeddings, retrieval and function calling

punkpeye/awesome-mcp-servers.what_it_does: A curated list of Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers that connect AI assistants to tools, data sources and services, organised by category.
punkpeye/awesome-mcp-servers.why_it_matters: It is the main discovery index for MCP servers, so it helps you find one before you build your own.
punkpeye/awesome-mcp-servers.when_to_use: When you are looking for an existing MCP server for a service or data source.

tesseract-ocr/tesseract.what_it_does: Tesseract is an open-source OCR engine that recognises text in images across many languages. It is a command-line tool and a library.
tesseract-ocr/tesseract.why_it_matters: It is a long-established open OCR engine and a common default in document pipelines.
tesseract-ocr/tesseract.when_to_use: When you need text from scanned pages or images with a mature, widely supported engine.

microsoft/markitdown.what_it_does: MarkItDown is a Python tool from Microsoft that converts files and office documents such as PDF, Word, Excel and PowerPoint into Markdown for LLM input.
microsoft/markitdown.why_it_matters: It handles the document-to-text step that many LLM pipelines need, in one small tool.
microsoft/markitdown.when_to_use: When you want to feed office documents or PDFs to a model as plain Markdown.

significant-gravitas/autogpt.what_it_does: AutoGPT is an open-source project for building and running autonomous AI agents, with a visual builder and a platform for hosting agents.
significant-gravitas/autogpt.why_it_matters: It was an early and very visible project in the autonomous-agent wave of 2023.
significant-gravitas/autogpt.when_to_use: When you want to experiment with a long-running agent platform or study an early open agent design.

n8n-io/n8n.what_it_does: n8n is a fair-code workflow automation platform. It connects hundreds of services with a visual builder and adds AI nodes for LLM and agent steps.
n8n-io/n8n.why_it_matters: It lets teams combine AI steps with ordinary automation in one tool, and it can be self-hosted.
n8n-io/n8n.when_to_use: When an AI step needs to sit inside a broader automation with many third-party integrations.

firecrawl/firecrawl.what_it_does: Firecrawl turns websites into clean Markdown or structured data through an API and an open-source server, for use by LLMs and agents.
firecrawl/firecrawl.why_it_matters: It is a widely used way to get web content into a RAG or agent pipeline without building a crawler.
firecrawl/firecrawl.when_to_use: When you need reliable web content for models at scale and prefer an API or a self-hosted server.

tauricresearch/tradingagents.what_it_does: TradingAgents is a multi-agent framework that uses LLM agents with different roles, such as analysts, researchers and a trader, to reason about financial trading decisions.
tauricresearch/tradingagents.why_it_matters: It is a well-known example of role-based multi-agent design applied to finance.
tauricresearch/tradingagents.when_to_use: When you want to study or experiment with multi-agent LLM designs for financial analysis. It is a research framework, not financial advice.

deepseek-ai/deepseek-r1.what_it_does: DeepSeek-R1 is an open-weight reasoning model that is trained to produce step-by-step reasoning before its answer. The repository holds the model card, papers and distilled variants.
deepseek-ai/deepseek-r1.why_it_matters: It is a widely used open reasoning model that shows the approach can be replicated with open weights.
deepseek-ai/deepseek-r1.when_to_use: When you need a reasoning-focused open model for maths, code or analysis tasks that you can run or fine-tune.

deepseek-ai/deepseek-v3.what_it_does: DeepSeek-V3 is an open-weight mixture-of-experts language model. The repository holds the model card, technical report and inference instructions.
deepseek-ai/deepseek-v3.why_it_matters: It is a large open model that competes with proprietary frontier models on many benchmarks.
deepseek-ai/deepseek-v3.when_to_use: When you need a strong general-purpose open model and have the hardware or a hosted endpoint to run it.
